rich_narrative.summary: The Muslim Academy of Greater Orlando provides Pre-K through 8th-grade private education focused on virtue, wisdom, and academic development <cite id="3">in Florida</cite>. In FY2025, the organization reported <cite id="1">Total Revenue of $3,145,617</cite>, down from $3,572,587 in FY2024. Despite its established local presence, the school is limited by key structural factors, including an unproven impact strategy and a lack of published board governance details. In FY2025 filings, the school posted a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 67.8%</cite> (67.8%), which falls below the 75% industry benchmark and leaves nearly a third of spending for administrative and operational costs. On the financial stability side, the academy holds <cite id="2">15.6 months of working capital</cite>, offering strong short-term liquidity. However, the organization lacks a documented theory of change and provides no publicly available beneficiary cost-efficiency tracking, restricting its broader appeal to impact-focused givers.
